summary: Each position's 512-dim vector is expanded to 2048 dims by a linear layer, passed through ReLU, and projected back to 512 dims, with the same weights at every position (Eq. 2); the residual add and LayerNorm sit outside this block, and dropout is applied only after the block, per Section 5.4.

blocks.label: Input x
blocks.description: The normalized output of the self-attention sub-layer, one 512-dim vector per position.
blocks.source_quote: In addition to attention sub-layers, each of the layers in our encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network, which is applied to each position separately and identically.

blocks.label: Linear W1 (expand)
blocks.description: Projects each position independently from d_model = 512 up to the inner dimension d_ff = 2048.
blocks.source_quote: The dimensionality of input and output is d model = 512 , and the inner-layer has dimensionality d f f = 2048 .

blocks.label: ReLU
blocks.description: Zeroes negative values elementwise, giving the network its nonlinearity.
blocks.source_quote: This consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between.

blocks.label: Linear W2 (project back)
blocks.description: Projects back down to d_model = 512 so the residual connection can add it to x.
blocks.source_quote: Another way of describing this is as two convolutions with kernel size 1.

blocks.label: FFN(x)
blocks.description: The sub-layer output, which goes on to dropout and then to encoder_add_norm_2 for the residual add and LayerNorm.
blocks.source_quote: While the linear transformations are the same across different positions, they use different parameters from layer to layer.
